title: Labyrinth
build: Two-sided English disk edition; stored credit at $743D-$747D includes V 1.0 V; supplied G64 preservation images

records.c: Sixty-four map cells read by $4173 in the captured mode. Columns 8,15,24,30,35,41,50,58 translate to type ten with depth limit32 and nonnegative boundary flag. Other cells among these64 resolve to type zero for the bound lookup, with limit24 and negative boundary flag. The map repeats through mask $5E=$3F; this is a world-coordinate strip, not screen pixels or a full collision simulator.

Sixteen translations of a map cell's low nibble. The captured type-four/five/seven/eight/nine/ten/eleven/twelve entries select type ten, while nibble two/three are negative; $4173 uses zero as their fallback depth-table index.

Sixteen inclusive upper column bounds for $4115: 8,15,24,30,35,40,50,255 followed by255. Opening column41 therefore selects region six; opening35 selects region four. These regions select a route entry after the bank is chosen.

Sixteen selectors for exit regions: first eight are three, then eight zeros. Selector at least three uses the shared PRNG high byte masked with $60, selecting bank offsets0,32,64,96. These numbers select an entry bank, not another room by themselves.
Bank-zero destination scenes, first eight three followed by zeros. Other banks' scene arrays begin $079E,$07BE,$07DE. Scene three is the captured Brick Hallway resource.
Sixteen target entry numbers for bank zero, beginning8,34,28,24,38,2,11,43. Entry identifiers belong to the target scene; they are not scene numbers.
Bank-one destination scenes, first eight three followed by zeros, selected at offset32 from $077E.
Bank-one entry identifiers beginning35,27,22,40,3,12,44,9, selected at offset32 from $078E.
Bank-two destination scenes, first eight three followed by zeros, selected at offset64 from $077E.
Bank-two entry identifiers beginning25,21,41,5,2,34,11,37, selected at offset64 from $078E.
Bank-three destination scenes, first eight three followed by zeros, selected at offset96 from $077E.
Bank-three entry identifiers beginning19,43,6,3,35,12,38,24, selected at offset96 from $078E.

Tail of movement processing. A negative map byte $B7 requests an exit immediately. Otherwise positive $028F advances depth $0544 toward $B2 using $DE and calls $3772 on a further attempt at the limit. Negative $028F subtracts $DE; underflow clears $0548/$0544/$0540. The later checks clamp a nonnegative low depth with zero high byte; a negative low depth instead calls $4115. Pose/drawing effects outside these checks remain unanalysed.

When $0385 is negative, consult $B3: negative blocks the exit call and nonnegative calls $4115. When $0385 is nonnegative, world X at least 80 bypasses that flag check. The captured ordinary approach uses $0385=$FF. Continuation at $378F handles standing/wall behavior; type-specific effects following $3796 are only partly traced.

In negative $0343 map mode, choose the first $074E threshold at least as large as column $AF, scanning indices zero through fourteen and falling back to fifteen. Read its selector at $076E: zero selects bank zero; one/two use $0500/$0501; at least three calls PRNG $4210. Mask the result with $60, OR the threshold index, then read entry at $078E and scene at $077E into $0532/$0530. The first corridor's reachable opening columns use selectors three and scene three in every bank. Nonnegative mode instead copies fixed $0345/$0346. This dispatcher selects a target; it does not load it or prove a wall opening is reachable.
Temporary index selected by $4115; runtime value rather than a route-table entry.
Set Y zero and enter $4173. The natural corridor has $0343=$FF and $5E=$3F, so the resulting column repeats every 4096 world-coordinate units.

In negative $0343 mode, shift the X-coordinate pair at $0538,Y/$053C,Y left twice and mask its high byte with $5E into $AF. Read map cell $0600,X, retain it at $B7, translate its low nibble through $073E into $B0, and use type zero for a negative translated type when selecting depth limit $B2 from $41F0 and auxiliary bound flag $B3 from $4200. Other modes use scene callbacks and update $341A; the page covers the captured negative map mode.

Sixteen depth bounds indexed by the translated map type, with negative types falling back to entry zero. In the captured corridor, ordinary wall cells resolve to bound 24 and opening type ten resolves to bound 32.

Sixteen auxiliary bytes selected alongside $41F0. The captured corridor's ordinary wall type zero is $FF and opening type ten is zero. At $3772, when $0385 is negative, a negative flag blocks the exit call and a nonnegative flag permits it.

Update the 16-bit seed at $0502/$0503 to (37*seed+17) modulo 65536 and return its high byte in A. Exit selector values at least three use returned bits five/six to choose one of four route banks. Other callers can advance this shared sequence, so a player route alone does not fix the variant.

For slots two down to zero, skip entry $FF at $5080,X. With nonnegative mode $26, split the entry into coordinate high/low by two LSR/ROR pairs, giving world X = 64*entry+32; set depth six for player slot zero and 24 for other slots. Clear fractional/depth-high fields, set origin/projected coordinates and active flags, then clear entry request $0532. Negative-mode grid/graph placement branches are retained here but not covered by the corridor widget. A natural scene-three load reached this routine with entries [35,255,26] and mode zero, then placed the player at X 2272/depth six. Bytes $543A-$54CB match between the corridor image and natural Brick Hallway image.
